subject: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements / FintechCo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements / FintechCo

Hi Alex / Lydia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points you called out
- PII in prompts and responses: regulatory requirement to redact or avoid storing direct identifiers in logs.
- Auditability: compliance team needs exportable, tamper-evident audit logs for all inference requests (structured, timestamped).
- Retention controls: must be able to set short retention windows (30 days or less) per environment/route.
- Selective logging: ability to disable or mask logs for specific routes (e.g., auth-related flows).

Current stack notes (from call)
- Front end -> API Gateway -> AWS Lambda -> internal services (Postgres)
- HubSpot for CRM; security reviews handled by internal Security Ops (Lydia)

Success criteria for POC
- Proof that we can ingest traffic and not persist raw PII in logs (redaction or tokenization)
- Exportable audit logs in JSON to S3 for 90/30-day retention policy (you mentioned target 30 days)
- Demonstrate per-route logging control + ability to disable raw request bodies
- Performance within acceptable bounds (<250ms tail for small prompts)

What Redwood can deliver (high level)
- Configurable retention per workspace/route (0–365 days) with automatic expiration and optional S3 export.
- Audit logs available as structured JSON with built-in redaction hooks; option to write either masked records or hashed identifiers.
- Route-level logging toggles and programmatic controls via API/SDK.
- KMS/HSM integration for keys; SOC 2 artifacts and an overview of logging architecture attached.

Next steps
1) I’ll send the SOC 2 summary + logging overview (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your engineering + our security engineer (Monica) — propose next Tue/Thu.
3) Share a draft mutual action plan / SOW for initial POC (Drive link to follow).

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, redwood-data-logging-overview.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap, that covers most of it. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Retention: our compliance policy currently requires 30 days maximum for any PII-containing logs. Can Redwood guarantee workspace-level retention down to 30 days (or less)?
- Redaction timing: do you offer redaction at tokenization time (before logs are written) or post-generation redaction? We prefer not to persist raw prompt/response bodies at any point.
- Export: we need the ability to export audit logs to our S3 bucket on a daily basis; can you push to customer-managed S3 or do we need to pull?

Security contact for technical deep dive will be Lydia (cc’d).

Also, can you share a sample of the logging schema (fields, pseudonymization approach)?

Thanks — Alex

Alex —

Great questions — quick answers below, and I’ve attached a sample logging config JSON as promised. Monica (cc) will join the technical deep dive to walk through the schema.

- Retention: yes — Redwood supports workspace- and route-level retention policies down to 0 days. We can enforce a 30-day maximum for any routes you flag as PII-sensitive. Expired logs are deleted automatically; we also support daily export to customer S3 for archival before deletion.

- Redaction timing: we support both approaches. For strict compliance you can enable pre-persistence redaction/tokenization via our ingest hooks so raw text is not written to persistent logs. Alternatively, we can store masked records where sensitive tokens are replaced with hashed identifiers. We will not require you to persist raw prompts/responses.

- Export: we can push directly to a customer-managed S3 bucket via IAM role we request, or you can pull from our export endpoint — both are supported. We typically recommend push-to-customer-S3 for stronger ownership and auditability.

- Logging schema: audit logs are structured JSON with fields like timestamp, route_id, workspace_id, request_hash, redaction_status, action, and optionally masked_tokens. Monica will share the full schema during the tech call.

Next steps (updated)
- Monica to propose 2 windows for a 60-minute technical deep-dive (we can do Tue 12/8 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 12/10 1:00–2:00 PT).
- I’ll share the draft mutual action plan in Drive and a sample logging config (attached).
- If acceptable, we can spin up a POC workspace and provide instructions for setting up S3 export and retention policies.

Attachment: redwood-logging-config-sample.json

Thanks!
